claims.text: High configurational disorder in high-entropy alloys consists of a random distribution of multiple principal elements.
High configurational disorder creates a heterogeneous distribution of atomic bond strengths.
The heterogeneous distribution of bond strengths impedes dislocation nucleation under sliding wear.
The heterogeneous distribution of bond strengths impedes dislocation propagation under sliding wear.
Disorder-induced inhibition of dislocation dynamics is key to the wear resistance of high-entropy-alloy coatings.
The proposed baseline is a fully disordered, equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy-alloy coating with no deliberately imposed short-range order.
The controlled intervention increases local atomic order while keeping overall composition constant.
Annealing or an ordering-promoting simulation parameter can be used to increase short-range order.
Chemical disorder and local ordering produce different spatial distributions of bond strengths and local coordination environments.
A wide distribution of bond strengths creates local energy barriers to coordinated dislocation motion.
Increasing short-range order reduces bond-strength heterogeneity.
Reduced bond-strength heterogeneity lowers barriers to dislocation motion.
Lower barriers facilitate dislocation propagation and thereby reduce wear resistance.
Under otherwise identical simulated wear conditions, the disordered baseline will have a lower dislocation-nucleation rate than the more ordered case.
Under otherwise identical simulated wear conditions, dislocations will propagate more slowly in the disordered baseline than in the more ordered case.
The increased-short-range-order case will exhibit greater dislocation activity and more simulated wear than the disordered baseline.

The proposed relationship applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic multiple-principal-element alloys when temperature and strain rate do not induce phase transformations or other dominant high-temperature wear effects.

Failure of increased short-range order to produce a statistically significant increase in both dislocation activity and simulated wear, or observation of improved performance, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
